title: The vaulted nave — Gothic cathedral interior

subject.summary: An interior-first, six-bay Gothic nave: paired clustered piers carry pointed arcades, a triforium and high clerestories beneath a luminous ribbed vault; a twelve-light rose terminates the long perspective. Generic designed reconstruction, not an identified cathedral or a surveyed building. All dimensions, bay counts, tracery and furnishings are inferred design choices; dust and light effects are decorative.

sources.title: Public-showcase cathedral hologram request
sources.ref: The nave of a gothic cathedral seen from inside: two rows of piers with pointed arches, a ribbed vault overhead, clerestory windows and a rose window at the far end.

facts.value: Transverse pointed ribs, crossing diagonal ribs, longitudinal ridge and simplified continuous pointed web shell
facts.note: A legible ribbed-vault interpretation. Thin web geometry simplifies masonry curvature and does not claim authentic quadripartite stereotomy.

facts.value: Paired lancets and a small oculus inside each high pointed opening; blind triplet triforium below
facts.note: A designed Gothic elevation hierarchy added to make the requested interior intelligible.

facts.value: Twelve radial lights, petalled tracery, central roundel and an annular stone surround; centre 20 m above the floor
facts.note: Invented geometric tracery, not copied or authenticated stained glass. No saint, donor, date, dedication or cathedral identity is asserted.

facts.value: Two narrow side aisles with lower pointed transverse vault ribs and lancet openings
facts.note: Secondary spaces chosen to give the two nave arcades believable depth and support.

facts.value: Three shallow sanctuary steps, a plain altar and two tall candle stands
facts.note: Restrained designed furnishings for scale; their presence is not evidence about a specific church.

facts.value: Small open joints between adjacent repeated masonry panels
facts.note: Masonry-panel joints preserve legibility without coincident wireframe edges.
